title: Chanan HaNechba
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: [Taanit 23b](https://www.sefaria.org/Taanit.23b.8) relates that he was the daughter’s son of Choni HaMe’agel and was very pious. When rain was needed, the Rabbis would send the schoolchildren to him; they would take hold of the hem of his cloak and say to him, “Father, father, give us rain.” He said before the Holy One, blessed be He: “Master of the world, do it for the sake of these, who cannot distinguish between the Father who gives rain and the father who does not give rain.” Why was he called Chanan HaNechba? Because he used to hide himself in the privy. Hyman explains that he was very modest there. [Rabbeinu Chananel](https://www.sefaria.org/Rabbeinu_Chananel_on_Taanit.23b.1) gives another explanation: “We have a tradition that the sages sought to appoint him leader over the community, and he did not accept; he went and hid, therefore they called him Chanan HaNechba.” [Seder HaDorot](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1403&lang=en) cites this from Jerusalem Talmud Ketubot, chapter 2, but Hyman says he did not find it in the Jerusalem Talmud text he used.[^1]

notes.text: The linked Bavli has Chanan; Rabbeinu Chananel writes Chanin and connects the nickname to hiding after he refused a leadership role. Heilprin attributes that explanation to Jerusalem Talmud Ketubot, chapter 2. Hyman says he did not find it in the Jerusalem Talmud text he consulted.
